quest.title: As Though Beholding Illusions
quest.description: Strange phenomena have suddenly appeared near the venue for the Mikawa Flower Festival. Dark undercurrents seem to be forming...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.num: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Second Night
chapter.title: As Though Beholding Illusions

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: As I said, let's wait until midnight. You can attend to other matters in the meantime.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Doesn't look like Miko is around here anywhere. Paimon doesn't see Ayato or Ayaka, either...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are we too early? Hmm... Didn't Ayato say he prepared lodging for everyone at the shrine?

dialogues.speaker: Senga
dialogues.text: ...Did you hear? Someone encountered a doppelganger here last night!

dialogues.speaker: Wakana
dialogues.text: A doppelganger!? You mean... like a doppelganger of themselves, or someone they know?

dialogues.speaker: Takitoh
dialogues.text: You know what they say... Anyone who sees their doppelganger will be replaced by them within three days..

dialogues.speaker: Wakana
dialogues.text: Th—That's just a folk tale! It's not real!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #...Doppelgangers? That's a common folk tale in Inazuma, isn't it... Ever heard of it, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I know the gist.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, it's a pretty famous one, huh... A friend being replaced by a complete stranger!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Also, the timing is a bit too coincidental, don't you think? Could it be related to what we saw last night?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The whole doppelganger thing sounds kind of like what Sayu was talking about with Bunshin Phantasm... Maybe something went wrong with Kichiboushi's powers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Thinking about it isn't going to get us anywhere. Why don't we go check on Sayu's team?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... They're not here yet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe they're still asleep?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, if it's Sayu we're talking about, that's definitely possible... Oh, someone's coming!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Weird... Is he here to work on the equipment? But, he doesn't look like any of the workers we saw yesterday... And, it doesn't seem like he's here for the games...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah... He snuck away again! Do you think he might be...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's follow him and see what he does.

choices.text: No, never.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? It always comes up in light novels... You've really never seen it? It's like when your friend is replaced by a complete stranger!

talks.objective: Go to the area outside the venue

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You quietly follow the man out of the festival grounds...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's constantly looking back... Paimon's calling it now! Something fishy is going on!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't jump to conclusions. Let's keep watching.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good point! He could be on his way to meet someone! Let the hunter become the hunted!
...Reporting back, Ma'am. Nothing suspicious to note at the Bunshin Phantasm booth. It's possible there's no connection to the incident from last night.
I see... Did you find any other clues?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sara!?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Ah, good morning, you two.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heizou!? What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: I was wondering who was daring enough to sneak up on one of our detectives. Maybe I should have expected it to be you.

choices.text: I guess that makes us "the hunted."

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon...

response.speaker: Tenryou Commission Member
response.text: F—Forgive me, ma'am! I have failed as a detective... I... I did not realize someone was on my tail...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: #...Considering {NICKNAME}'s skill, the fault is not with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... So, what's going on? What are you investigating? It must be serious if Heizou's involved...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Well, about that... hehe...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...Unfortunately... My orders prevent me from sharing that information with you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What orders? You really can't tell us anything?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (If Sara and Heizou are so hesitant to divulge information... There's only one person who could be responsible.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Those orders come from the Shogun, don't they...
#An astute observation, {NICKNAME}... Tell {M#him}{F#her} the truth.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Sh—Shogun...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? The Shogun is here?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: No... I believe this is Ei.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...You recognized me with a single glance?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Shogun, we still haven't completed the investigation...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #It matters not. I am certain the person standing before us is our friend, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #{M#His}{F#Her} gaze, {M#his}{F#her} presence, {M#his}{F#her} mastery of several types of Elemental Energy... There is no mistake. And, we need {M#his}{F#her} help.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...Understood. An investigation team was sent to survey a piece of land. Yesterday, the Tenryou Commission received a report that the team was found unconscious in the field.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...Not only that, but the group appeared to have become trapped in an endless nightmare, unable to wake up.

response.speaker: Investigator Trapped in a Nightmare
response.text: N—No, please!

response.speaker: Investigator Trapped in a Nightmare
response.text: Stay away!

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: We detected intermittent traces of youkai power where they were found. We followed the traces and ended up here, just outside the festival grounds.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Should we call off the festival?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: Unfortunately, it's not that simple. You've heard the rumors about the doppelgangers, yes?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: We suspect the culprit has the ability to change form, allowing them to spread misinformation at will. They may have already infiltrated the festival grounds.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: If we call off the festival, we may give them a chance to escape amid the chaos...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Even the slightest movement could alert them. Locking down the festival grounds could provoke them to attack, which would endanger the public.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... That's a big risk...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The purpose of festival is to bring humans and youkai together. We cannot allow the culprit to endanger anyone.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, what if they attack again?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: A very valid concern. Last night, we dispatched a group of soldiers to the festival grounds. They'll remain undercover to keep an eye on things.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: We also blocked off several nearby roads under the pretext of construction, so we can keep civilians away as much as possible.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...Even the Almighty Shogun has taken it upon herself to patrol the area all night.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Fortunately, no one else has been harmed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah! So the thunder we heard was you!

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...I apologize for our failings, Shogun. You should not have had to intervene.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: On the contrary, it was my decision. I was unable to capture the culprit last night, so I left to discuss a plan with Miko. I did not show myself once I saw you were safe, and for that, I apologize.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, speaking of Miko... Where is she?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...She is investigating the trace of youkai power found at the scene. Though it fades in and out, it never strays from Mt. Yougou.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Which means... if the culprit infiltrated the festival grounds, they must still be nearby.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: The only people close to the grounds last night were the staff and the contestants staying at the shrine.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Miko is working with the Kamisato siblings to verify the identities of the staff members. They should be done soon.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: As for the contestants... That inquiry must be performed by someone else.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Is that why you need my help?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...The Tenryou Commission is too conspicuous. But as the judge of the competition, you can ask questions without arousing suspicion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so you need us to talk to the teams and see if there's an imposter among us...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #Precisely. {NICKNAME}, I understand these people are your friends, and it puts you in a difficult position...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But, if one of them has indeed been displaced by a youkai, they could be in grave danger...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I understand. I'll do my best.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Thank you. I truly hope the situation is not as grave as it seems.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are you guys gonna do next? Continue to investigate from a distance?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Well, there's only so much we can learn that way, so I think we need to find a way to slip onto the grounds. It's better for us to be at the scene if something goes wrong.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: I fear the Shogun is far too revered a figure for that. If she arrives at the grounds, it will certainly cause a stir.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Worry not. Miko and I discussed that issue. She claims to have a plan. The preparations are underway as we speak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: One of her genius plans, huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Somehow, "scheme" seems more accurate...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Indeed. If you learn any details of said plan, I would like to know what I'm getting myself into.

choices.text: So, the Tenryou Commission's on the case.

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: *yawn*... So tired... I don't feel rested at all. How come you two have so much energy? Didn't you stay up even later than me...?

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Haha, weak!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Kichiboushi! That's not a nice thing to say to a friend. Sayu's probably just tired because she came up with all the ideas yesterday!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Need a break, Sayu? I can start thinking about the ending stages in the meantime!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: It's been forever since we've done something fun together! You need to have enough energy to enjoy it!

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... I—It's okay... I can push through...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sayu and Yoimiya seem the same as ever! Kichiboushi, too. How should we test them...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's ask about the past...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, good idea! Doppelgangers only mimic appearances — they wouldn't know about someone's past! Let's give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Mm! White Fur! Yellow Fur!

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Whoa, you guys are here bright and early!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Y—Yeah, well... {NICKNAME}'s judging this thing, so we can't slack off... right?

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Still... You don't need to make anything, so what's the rush?

dialogues.speaker: Sayu
dialogues.text: Yeah... If the people in charge are here early, that usually means there's been some kind of emergency...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, no... It's just... {NICKNAME} really wanted to see you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Seriously, Paimon...?)

dialogues.speaker: Yoimiya
dialogues.text: Oh, um... Why?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... Well... It's... your game! Playing your game yesterday brought up a whole bunch of old memories!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, we wanted to come early to reminisce about old times, hehe. Y'know, because you might be busy... later... and stuff...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What kind of an excuse is that? They're busy now!)

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: White Fur... Acting super strange!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Time to change the topic!)

choices.text: Oh, I was just thinking about the Aranara...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, you know what? Me too! I thought about adding them to our game, considering the "dream" theme and everything.

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: But, in the end, the ideas just wouldn't come together...

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Marinara... Yum!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: No, it's not a food! The Aranara are like, um... small youkai from Sumeru. They're super friendly and cute, and can give you good dreams...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Actually, that describes you, too, Kichiboushi. If you ever go to Sumeru, I'm sure you'll be considered a "good Nara"!

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: ...Good banana?

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Sumeru, huh... The dreams there are supposed to be special. Did you witness a dream or something? Maybe it could give us some inspiration, and we wouldn't have to think so much...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: #Haha... Sorry, that dream is a little... hard to describe, don't you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sometimes, when there are too many feelings in a dream...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's really hard to use as reference material.

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Alright... *sigh* I was just wondering what kind of dream it was, that's all...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: I guess it was the kind where... a lot of things happened! Anyway, it's a long story. How about we wait until after the competition?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: #...{NICKNAME} and I can tell it together.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds good.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After that, you share many more memories together...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Oh, shoot, where did the time go... We have so many levels to design today!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, we should get out of your fur— hair, then! Good luck, everyone!

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Bye, White Fur! Bye, Yellow Fur! Come back and play!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, we've had so many adventures, huh... You don't even realize it until someone brings up the past.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Do you still remember the original meaning of our journey?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, yeah, totally! It was, um... What was it again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I figured...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, Paimon didn't pick up on anything suspicious from that team... If anything, we were the weird ones, forcing conversations and stuff...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And whose fault is that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Okay, so maybe it wasn't the best strategy. Leaning into the "judge" angle is probably a safer bet...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's ask about the creative process behind the game and confirm their identities that way... Paimon saw Thoma's team show up just now. So, we can investigate them next!

choices.text: Oh, I was just reminded of a certain ambush order...

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Huh? Wh—Why are you bringing that up all of a sudden?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, all the bake-danuki transformations...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Reminded of the time you failed that ninjutsu technique...

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Uh... Well, that was my bad... I tried to turn into a barrel, but my tail was sticking out... So, you found me immediately.

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: B—But this time, I'm not in charge of turning into things anymore, so it should be fine! I think...

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Haha, weak!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Kichiboushi, what did I say about talking that way...? Anyway, you seemed to have a good grasp on transformations yesterday, Sayu... What's the story here...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It all started with a certain mysterious order...

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Th—That one shouldn't be on me! I didn't realize I was tricked until later... Did all that work, and didn't even get to nap... Really shouldn't have taken that order...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Still... we had some fun times together, right?

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Umm...

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Based on what happened, I guess... You could say that...

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Whoa, I've never seen this look on Sayu's face... What the heck happened back then!?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mujina, is all red!

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: No, I'm not! And, I'm not a Mujina!

choices.text: Oh, I was just reminded of some pilgrimage training...

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mm! Had fun with Yellow Fur!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We went to soooooo many places together!

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Snowy mountain! Cold! Alcor! Big!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Wow, you traveled to all those places together?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Orange Fur come with next time?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: You betcha! You should come, too, Sayu! If you can find the time, of course!

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: Um... Would we have to walk there?

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: Nope! You can just sit on the boat and listen to stories. We'd be there before you knew it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can nap on the boat, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let the waves rock you to sleep.

response.speaker: Sayu
response.text: R—Really?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: As long as Storm-Storm not mad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! It's not like Dvalin's the one behind every single gust of wind!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Thoma! We were hoping to learn a bit more about the philosophy behind your game. Is now a good time?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Ah, looks like our judges are hard at work this morning.

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: ...Feel a soft bee?

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Oh, um... Boss can explain that one.

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: Boss and Shousei were up super late last night coming up with ideas!

dialogues.speaker: Kappa
dialogues.text: And, he's back at it this morning, as energetic as ever! Boss is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Oh, I don't deserve that much praise... But, when it comes to the "talking" part, I guess I'm the best person to answer your questions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe... Time for an interview!

dialogues.speaker: "Shousei"
dialogues.text: Into you...?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Ask away, judges!

choices.text: What do you think is the most interesting aspect of your game?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Oh, I'd have to say... working with others to overcome challenges...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hold on! You can't ask such a simple question, {NICKNAME}! Watch and learn...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *ahem*... We'd love to learn more about your design approach and strategic vision. What will be the project's main draw, and how will it deliver emotional value to your players?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (That's basically the same question...)

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Sounds like you took that question straight from one of those business experts in Ritou... In that case, let me say this...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: This product will be a fast-paced, easy-to-digest release that capitalizes on the enduring popularity of a traditional genre while addressing its common pain points...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: By reviewing our strengths and the needs of our players, we were able to synchronize them across production levels and provide a refined experience that is more receptive to our users and more enjoyable overall...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Impressive! And... completely over Paimon's head!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (You set yourself up for that one, Paimon!)

response.speaker: Kappa
response.text: Nice one, Boss!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha... I kind of confused myself, honestly. I'm used to hearing that kind of talk in Ritou, so I guess I picked up a few things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #A fixer is a tough nut to crack, huh... Shoot, Paimon can't pick apart an answer she doesn't understand! Over to you, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You continue asking questions, and Thoma answers faultlessly...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: ...So, there you have it. I hope that answered your question, judges.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... Not a single stumper...

choices.text: Impressive!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, well, I'm sure the interview is only one part of the evaluation process. We'll see what you think when you play the game yourself.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Which reminds me, I should probably get back to work on this stage. Wanna give it a try when we're done?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It would be my pleasure.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: In that case, let's get to it!

response.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
response.text: Y—Yes, Boss Thoma!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... Thoma's answers were all very genuine. Paimon didn't notice anything un-Thomalike about them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, he was with Shousei until late last night... If you think about when we saw the nightmare creature, the timing doesn't match up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Kozou and his two friends were together the whole time, too. They would have noticed if someone was acting weird.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So, we're back at square one! *sigh*... That just leaves Kokomi's team, right? Guess we should check them out...

choices.text: Never underestimate a housekeeper!
Did you design this game with anyone in mind?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Well... From a design standpoint, we want it to be a game for everyone...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Not so fast! "Everyone" isn't an answer! You need to be more specific about your target audience!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Ah... You're absolutely right. Then, allow me to revise my answer. Our target audience includes growing children, ages zero to eighteen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Makes sense! Kids need a little exercise here and there!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Second would be active adults, ages eighteen to forty.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! Adults have more stamina, so they can get more out of the game.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Next would be older adults, ages forty to sixty, especially those in need of exercise.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Older adults... Hm, exercise is important for healthy aging, but something feels off about this...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Finally, we have elderly people who are still full of life. That would be the sixty to a thousand age range.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, okay... Wait! That includes everyone!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha, well, we can't forget about the youkai, right? This game is for humans and youkai alike, after all.

response.speaker: "Shousei"
response.text: But, not for Ioroi!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Because he's trapped in a statue, I'm guessing...?)

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Besides, you seemed to agree with each group, Paimon... Unless you intend to change your tune?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *ahem*... N—Next question!

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Huh? White Fur and Yellow Fur are here early!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're here alone? Huh... Where are Kokomi and the others?

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Don't know about great youkai, but sole lady is behind you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sole lady? Oh, as in "Sole of the Deep"? Okay... Wait, did you say behind us!?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: You have questions for me, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: K—Kokomi! A little warning next time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Sounds like you already know why we're here.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Yes, I heard about the Doppelganger incident. When I saw you around the venue just now, it wasn't hard to connect the dots.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: As for what you want to know...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: ...Energy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Energy...? Oh! The numbers you write in your diary—

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: ...In a tree? Dry berry?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: ...Ahem.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... S—Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: So... we can leave it there, right? You don't need to ask any more questions, I would imagine...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Y—Yep, all good.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: As for Gyoubu Koban... He was in the shrine all night. I can't imagine he's the criminal you're searching for.

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: EH!? Gyoubu Koban is a criminal!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: N—No, of course not! You're in the clear!

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Phew... "In the clear"... is good?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Very good.

dialogues.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
dialogues.text: Good!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about Mizuki? Where did she go?

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: She left after receiving a message in the middle of night... Looking back on it, perhaps it's related to your own investigation.

dialogues.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
dialogues.text: Oh, as she left, I heard her whisper under her breath, "Ordering me around in the middle of the night. Who does she think she is...?"

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Miko.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She probably needed an expert on nightmares to help formulate a strategy... Well, I guess that also confirms Mizuki's identity.)

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hm, something tells me a certain someone is missing me...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Miko! And Mizuki!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #*yawn*... Hello, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you finish up your work?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Yes, I left the rest to the young fellow from the Kamisato Clan. At least for now, there's nothing suspicious to note.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That means... the culprit didn't manage to sneak in? That's a relief...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Just like that, you let down your guard? And all it took was for me to wear her face...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...EH!? Th—The culprit! I—It's you!

choices.text: If you keep joking like this...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh? Greedy little thing... I thought we agreed on twenty?

choices.text: Making a joke like that...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #*sigh* It's getting harder and harder to tease you, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Can you stop with the teasing, then? Even I'm reaching my limit...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Five hundred years, and you're still not used to it? Sounds like you need more practice.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: At least spare me for the day. I can't take the mental torment right now. I'm running on fumes...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, what did you do last night...?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Investigated the Shogunate officials' nightmares, analyzed the traces of youkai power around Mt. Yougou... Oh, and worked on some new game stages, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All in one night!?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Well, I didn't want someone to ruin the Mikawa Flower Festival... But I also wanted to do my best for my part of the Festival.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Besides, I've talked to many patients who worked multiple jobs just to make ends meet. Compared to that, complaining about one night of hard work is a little... unreasonable, don't you think?

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: Even so, I think you should take a break, Miss Mizuki. Gyoubu Koban and I can handle the game development in the meantime.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: I learned a lot yesterday. I'm sure I can handle a few design elements while you get some rest.

response.speaker: Sangonomiya Kokomi
response.text: We can't have our lead developer out of commission. I'm not confident I can bring our vision to fruition on my own.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: You're very persuasive, Kokomi. It would seem you also have a talent for clinical psychology... I'll leave it to you two, then.

response.speaker: "Gyoubu Koban"
response.text: Sweet dreams!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Mizuki goes to rest. A little unsteady on her feet, she looks exhausted...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mizuki really cares about the festival, huh... She's putting so much pressure on herself...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...Perhaps she's reminded of the festivals of the past, when I was just a kit, and Mizuki a young baku.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...We would rush past the other youkai, desperate to get the first piece of Fried Tofu from the ramen stand.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmph, it would seem she hasn't forgotten, even after five hundred years.

choices.text: Sounds like you haven't forgotten, either...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...You know, there's something to be said for knowing when to keep your mouth shut, little one.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hmph... Enough about the past. We must focus on the matter at hand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... you didn't notice anything suspicious, right? That should mean the culprit didn't sneak in...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: That's one possibility. The other... is that the culprit's "transformation" is even more convincing than we imagined.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In that case, we need a "detective" with a more professional skillset... Or, we need to find a way to provoke them and get their facade to crack.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, that sounds dangerous!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: If the culprit is deep in disguise, a slight provocation won't completely expose them.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: What we need is to create reasonable doubt, make the culprit question whether their cover is blown... As they hesitate over whether to make some kind of last stand, that is our chance.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, how do you plan to provoke them?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, Ei didn't tell you? Hehe... Allow me to show you.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...Ladies and gentlemen, on behalf of the Mikawa Flower Festival, it is my honor to announce...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: An esteemed guest from Tenshukaku has agreed to take part in this year's festival!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Please welcome, Her Excellency, the Almighty Narukami Ogosho, God of Thunder!

response.speaker: Yoimiya
response.text: It... It's the Shogun!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: The Almighty Shogun... is here in person?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: So, this was your plan, Miko.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well? Not bad, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that was quite the entrance... Paimon can't believe she agreed to that...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...The Almighty Shogun's presence is bound to cause a stir. Instead of struggling to maintain a low profile, it's better for her to step into the open.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: And, it means a detective can slip into the venue alongside the retinue, without turning any heads at all.

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: In the presence of the Shogun, not even the most cunning of criminals can let down their guard. Their every move needs to be faultless.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: The more you focus on getting one thing right, the easier it is for the rest to become cracks in the glass...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's what Miko wants us to take advantage of...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: And, she's using the Almighty Shogun as bait... Hmph, the Lady Guuji is as daring as ever.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why didn't you clue us in earlier? We wasted all that time asking pointless questions...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Your intel was very useful, actually. We don't know how things will unfold, but I have a feeling the truth will be revealed soon.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: #In the meantime, stick with the Shogun, {NICKNAME}. We need everyone focused on her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll do my best...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...Alright. Under my command, the Tenryou Commission will remain on high alert. If anything goes wrong, report back to me at once.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (After that... We surveyed each stall, just like yesterday...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Ei's presence definitely caused a stir, but it didn't take long for the festive atmosphere to return...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Maybe a day will come when Ei can leave Tenshukaku, and it won't be so out of the ordinary.)

choices.text: (Remain silent...)
You're the only one in Inazuma who would do that.
I want thirty percent of the profit.

dialogues.speaker: Inoue
dialogues.text: ...A—Almighty Shogun! Glory to your everlasting reign... I—I mean... Welcome, welcome!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: This stall looks familiar. Yet, it would seem the ownership has changed hands...?

dialogues.speaker: Inoue
dialogues.text: Ah... You must be thinking of Tomoki. H—He... wasn't feeling well today, so I'm filling in... haha...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I see... Yet, you remind me of someone — a Doushin from the Tenryou Commission...

dialogues.speaker: Inoue
dialogues.text: Oh, uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you looking at, Ei?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Hm, the food offerings. Although, this vendor seems...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The "vendor" is giving me a pleading look... Judging by his cooking skill, it almost seems like his first day on the job...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ei... He's "working."

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Working...? Ah.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...I see. I appreciate your dedication, sir.

dialogues.speaker: Inoue
dialogues.text: O—Of course! It's an honor to serve such esteemed guests!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: No need for formalities... I'll take three orders of Dango Milk.

dialogues.speaker: Inoue
dialogues.text: ...Right away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Three orders? So, Paimon gets one, too?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Yes, I wanted to thank you for accompanying me. Without you by my side, I imagine the people here would be on edge even now.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I have my reasons for being here, of course, but I would hate to tarnish the festive atmosphere.

choices.text: This festival is for everyone.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Heh, indeed. The Mikawa Flower Festival... Hundreds of years have passed since I last partook in the festivities. Much is different this time — the people, the place, the games...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yet, the name endures, and the joy of celebration along with it... I suppose that, in itself, is a form of Eternity.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon... and the Almighty Shogun?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Mizuki! Looks like you got some much-needed rest!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Yumemizuki Mizuki... Thank you for your aid earlier.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Of course, I'm always willing to help. It's my duty... I wish I could have dispelled the nightmares, but this situation is uncharted territory for me.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Even so, relieving the pain of the nightmares is no small feat. You honor the legacy of the Yumekui-Baku.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, not even Mizuki could fix it... What's going on with this nightmare creature...?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Let's save the difficult questions for later. Actually, I came here to ask you something.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Wanna come to Aisa Bathhouse with me? Most of the contestants will be there... Oh, and don't worry about payment — it's my treat!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Yes! Yes! Let's go!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You want us to go to the hot springs... now?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Well, game development isn't easy. Most of the contestants are exhausted and could use a break.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: You've been under a lot of pressure yourselves, with the investigation and all. So, I thought you might like to join.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Of course we would! Right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...I will remain here. I rarely have time away from Tenshukaku, and I would like to continue perusing the stalls.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aw... That's too bad...

choices.text: Then, I'm not going, either...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #Ah, I almost forgot! Miko wanted to talk to you, {NICKNAME}. I'll take you to her first.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Oh? Well why don't we all go—

response.speaker: Inoue
response.text: Almighty Shogun! Your Dango Milk is ready...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh... Delicious!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: No need, Shogun! Miko just had some quick things to go over with the judges, that's all — you and Paimon can wait here. We'll only be a minute!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Be right back.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Alright, now we can talk freely.

choices.text: Miko doesn't need to see me, does she...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I think something's off with the Shogun. You've been with her the whole day. Have you noticed anything?

choices.text: S—Something off? No...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Up close, sometimes it's hard to see the whole picture... I think something is troubling her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Something did seem off with Ei today... Maybe she's not used to leaving Tenshukaku? Or was it the reaction of the crowd...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (No, we've been through so much. Something so trivial wouldn't shake her... She must be keeping something to herself...)

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I've witnessed a lot of cases where patients, for a variety of reasons, are unwilling or unable to seek help. Unfortunately, that only exacerbates the problem...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Until their emotions become so heavy, even the strongest of people collapse under the weight... I see those warning signs in the Shogun.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, even the archons aren't immune to emotional strain?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Humans, youkai, and archons bear the same capacity for emotion and are, naturally, susceptible to the same mental turmoil.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: It's very possible that someone who appears strong on the outside has learned to compartmentalize their negative emotions... And that is far from healthy.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I understand.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #Anyway, the quickest route to curing the mind is through the heart! That's where you come in, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: As a clinical psychologist, isn't that where YOU come in?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Approaching someone in a professional capacity often makes them more guarded. But, don't worry! You'll still have my help!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Here, with these two special coupons, you can get into Aisa Bathhouse after closing. Then, this is what you're gonna do...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Finally! You're back! Paimon's had two servings of Dango Milk already!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #Sorry for the wait... It sounds like {NICKNAME} has other plans, Paimon. So, we'll have to head to the bathhouse on our own.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? You're not coming...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll explain later... Just have fun!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay... Paimon will bring you back a Hot Spring Egg!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...There is no need to stay behind on my behalf. If you leave now, I'm sure you can catch up.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Something tells me YOU chose to stay behind on OUR behalf...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...What makes you say that?

choices.text: You want everyone to relax.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...If my presence makes them nervous or impedes their ability to relax, does that not defeat the purpose of going to the hot springs?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I already disturbed their progress by coming to the festival. The last thing everyone needs is more distractions.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...But, aren't you under pressure, too?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: As you know, this body is hardly that fragile. It can operate for another hundred years with no issue.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...You didn't deny it.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Hah. Mortals are weak in body and mind. If there is a choice of who to bear such a burden, naturally that person should be me.

choices.text: What if you didn't have to worry about bothering anyone...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: What does it matter? The world is not so easily bent to one's will...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'll take that as a yes.

choices.text: I have a pair of special coupons here...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #Heh, what clever verbal tricks, {NICKNAME}... It appears you've been spending too much time with Miko.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's an honest offer...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: You think you can get away with manipulating the Shogun? I wouldn't be so sure...

choices.text: ...C'mon, let's go!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: *sigh* Persistent indeed... Very well. As you proposed, we shall set out at midnight.

choices.text: You'll go, won't you?
We can get into the bathhouse after closing.
Would you agree to go to the hot springs then?
You don't want people to be on edge because of you.
Yeah, she seems troubled...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Exactly! You noticed, too...

choices.text: You needed to talk to me in private. Why?
Okay, I'll go...
Including you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Alright, no reason to delay.

talks.objective: Invite Ei to the Aisa Bathhouse
Talk to Ei in the Aisa Bathhouse

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...Steam replete with the scent of orchids. Water that turns the complexion a blushing pink... So, this is a hot spring.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it your first time here?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Yes, there are Royal Hot Springs near Tenshukaku. But, the plans were set in motion only after Hiiragi Hiroshi introduced the Snezhnayan Blast Furnace to Inazuma, and that was five hundred years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: When the project was complete, I was already in the Plane of Euthymia... And, naturally, the body of the Shogun has no need for such luxuries.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hiiragi Hiroshi...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: The members of the Kanjou Commission were once friends with Makoto and the Kitsune Saiguu. Although mere mortals, those who managed to survived back then were special individuals indeed.

choices.text: What happened back then?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...What makes you say that?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The look on your face...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Now I see why my officials claim that the hot springs facilitate conversation. Even I find myself divulging more than intended.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...You're correct. Following the dark disaster five hundred years ago, a Nightmare engulfed Inazuma.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: On a battlefield consumed in darkness, our soldiers fought against dark forces, creatures capable of possessing people and trapping them in nightmares. Even the Yumekui-Baku could do nothing to wake them.

choices.text: As awful as that sounds...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Perhaps not. The battle was intense. Those who stood up in defense of this land knew the chance of survival was slim. In the face of certain death, surely a nightmare is nothing to fear...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: But, what if I told you this... If the person trapped in the nightmare was strong enough to overcome incapacitation, it would become a waking nightmare instead.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The person would lose all capacity to distinguish dream from reality, perceiving everything in the real world as a continuation of the war.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: And every precious thing in life as an enemy to be annihilated... That is a far more painful nightmare, both for the person in question and those around them.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...If I hadn't broken out of the nightmare yesterday, would that have happened to me? Then, Ei must be so worried because...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Did that happen to someone... back then?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Yes.

choices.text: And...?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: I... unleashed Musou no Hitotachi and struck her down.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: No need. I have no regrets. I know it was the right decision, both for Inazuma's sake and her own.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: If necessary, I would do it again.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Ei...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Well, it's about time you two showed yourselves, yes? You've listened in long enough.
Heh.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh? It's you two.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Before you say anything, this part wasn't me.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well, since the cat's out of the bag...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: How about a hot spring tea party?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Hey!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ahhh... Nice and warm. No wonder the hot springs relaxed your inhibitions, Ei...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...So, who came up with this idea? I want the truth.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I guess... both of us?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Well, I happened to consult a certain clinical psychologist about how to get an old friend to open up...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: In her expert opinion, doing something new with a trusted companion in a new environment can make someone less guarded... Looks like it worked like a charm.

choices.text: I understand the reasoning...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: It's one thing to trust that Miko has good intentions, but would you let your guard down around her?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Good point.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Your concern is misplaced. I kept these matters to myself because I was unsure whether this incident is connected to the past, and I did not want to interfere with the investigation.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: If the investigation reached an impasse or new clues pointed to the Nightmare from back then... Naturally, I would have discussed this intel with you.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Intel, huh... It appears you still don't understand why I wanted you to open up in the first place.
Help! Help me!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was that!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Then, Ei must be so worried because...)

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Sounds like it came from outside. Let's check it out!

choices.text: But, why not do it yourself?
...I'm sorry.
What happened...?
It doesn't seem bad enough to make you this upset.
Does it have anything to do with what's happening right now?

talks.objective: Go to the area outside the Aisa Bathhouse

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh, no... Someone's unconscious!

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: Uh... Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it the Nightmare!?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: It seems different in some respects... Step back and allow me to examine her.

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: Ugh... Ah!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...She's awake?

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: What's going on... Ah! A—Almighty Shogun!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: What happened just now? What frightened you?

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: Sh—Shogun... I... I...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: It's alright. With the Shogun here, nothing can hurt you. Just take a deep breath and tell us what happened.

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: Phew... I almost fainted again just now...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that what happened earlier? You fainted?

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: Yes... I was on my way to Uyuu Restaurant, and as I was crossing the bridge, I saw someone staring at me from behind a tree!

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: It was hard to make out their appearance in the dark, but I had a bad feeling... So, I tried to get a closer look in the moonlight...

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: And, it was... It was me!

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: In that moment, I thought about how people who see their doppelganger usually end up dead, and I fainted from the shock... I don't remember anything after that...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: A doppelganger? In Inazuma City? But, we only detected traces of the Nightmare around Mt. Yougou...

dialogues.speaker: Rie
dialogues.text: I heard that people encountered doppelgangers on Mt. Yougou, too! C—Could it be the work of some terrible youkai?

choices.text: Don't worry about that...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Now that we have an understanding of the situation, why don't I take you to the Police Station to file a report?

response.speaker: Rie
response.text: O—Okay...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...The situation is getting worse. If the doppelganger is limited to the festival grounds, that's one thing... But, appearing on a random street in Inazuma City...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Hm... On the bright side, the victim seems okay this time...

response.speaker: Haruto
response.text: B—Bad news, Shogun!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Hm? A Tenryou Commission official... What's wrong?

response.speaker: Haruto
response.text: A—Another victim... at the... the festival... Kappa... Kappa is... trapped in a nightmare!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: What!?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But... Sara and the others were keeping watch!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Make haste! Back to Mt. Yougou at once!

choices.text: The strongest youkai in Inazuma are all right here.

talks.objective: Return to the venue on Mt. Yougou

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: That's right! Because of the folk tale about doppelgangers, the culprit was able to incite panic without attacking anyone at all...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: But, after the Tenryou commission secured the venue, the culprit appeared in Inazuma City so that the panic would spread.

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: But, what is the end goal? Panic doesn't seem like enough of a motive...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: You're right, panic is a means to an end. But, I think the shift to Inazuma City proves something... Whatever their goal, terrorizing one location wasn't enough...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: And, since Inazuma City is their new target, the person they're impersonating at the festival... should be absent...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Unless... the culprit found a way to cover their tracks and incite more panic...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: ...By leaving behind a "stand-in."

dialogues.speaker: Youko & Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Ahh—!

dialogues.speaker: Youko & Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: Ahh—!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: K—Kappa is... Kappa is made of wood!?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: No wonder I couldn't sense the nightmare!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I see... So, the doppelganger infiltrated the festival as Kappa and is currently hiding in Inazuma City... Is that correct?

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: ...Not just that. Replacing one person wasn't enough... If multiple people are replaced at once, they can cover for each other.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: ...We didn't get to see each other much during the Test of Courage...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kozou and his two friends were together the whole time, too. They would have noticed if someone was acting weird.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: This kind of transformation is said to have a particular weakness... If the subject is frightened, the disguise starts to crumble. Isn't that right, "Youko" and "Hitotsume Kozou"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...I—It's a bake-danuki tail!
Kinkaku! Ginkaku! Run!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku & Ginkaku
dialogues.text: ...T—Tetsunosuke!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku & Ginkaku
dialogues.text: ...T—Tetsunosuke!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *coughing*... Th—They're getting away!

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: Aren't you supposed to be in Inazuma City?

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: ...And leave you two by yourselves? That's not the Tanuki way!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: ...No fighting! Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Oh, you didn't go to the hot springs?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You didn't either?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Ah, well... A whole crowd of people have left already. I'll go a bit later with Shousei and a few others.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Besides, we're a bit behind with our game. We need to catch up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, your team is the biggest...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Haha, I guess it's my fault for going overboard with the ideas. Kozou and the others can barely keep up.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Sometimes delegating work is harder than doing it yourself... I wonder if this is how he feels, being the head of the clan.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, don't work too hard...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Of course! Right back at you!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like everyone's busy trying to finish their game... I should come back later.)

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: N—Nothing's working! The humans are catching up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Little rascals... Stop running!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: ...Hmph, you wish!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Well, Ioroi, as I see it, you've been punished long enough. It's about time you were released...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: R—R—Released!? I can do that myself any time I want! This statue keeps me warm in the winter and cool in the summer. Don't interfere!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku, Ginkaku, and Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Ioroi is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku, Ginkaku, and Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Ioroi is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku, Ginkaku, and Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Ioroi is the best!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...Besides, the seal's power is almost gone... What I really want is for you to help me give that sneaky kitsune a piece of my mind!

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Ioroi, she's already—

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Not so fast! I won't be fooled by your tricks again! Whatever you were about to say, she can tell me herself, instead of sending some young kitsune to hoodwink me!

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: That's right, the entities appeared at the same time and place. That's why the Tenryou Commission conflated the two at first.

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: But, if we ignore the nightmare creature and look at the doppelganger incident in isolation... the culprit's motive is clear.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like everyone's busy trying to finish their game... I should come back later.)

talks.objective: Talk to Kinkaku and the others

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: We... We're almost rid of them...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: ...That's enough! I will not fail the Shogun again because of you!

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: EH!!! A tengu!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: Tengu was flying... Tengu is a cheater!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Surrender now, and I will spare your life.

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Tengu... Why are you helping the humans! Tengu is a youkai!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: *scoff*... My loyalty is to the Shogun. Humans and youkai are no different in my eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: Shogun... That's the leader of the humans!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: ...Shogun sent people to steal our land... Shogun is bad!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Nonsense! The Shogun would never give such an order!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Calm yourself, Sara. Let's hear them out.

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Shogun... sent humans to steal our home...

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: And the Mikawa Flower Festival! Shogun is making youkai serve the humans...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Serve the humans? He's not talking about the game development, is he...?

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: *whimper*... Shogun even forced great baku youkai to work all night...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh... you mean yesterday? That was my choice, actually...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez, where are these ideas coming from?

choices.text: I think there are some misunderstandings...

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: S—Stay back!

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: Humans want to enslave us again!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Hold on, something's not right! We should try a different approach...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: No need... I know what's wrong. They're trapped in a nightmare.

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: What are you doing...!? Trying to put Tetsunosuke to work!?

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: G—Ginkaku... doesn't wanna stay up all night... *whimper*...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Servitude, enslavement... These might sound like ridiculous misunderstandings to us. But, that is their reality right now.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...A world of despair and fear, where enemies lurk at every turn... devoid of even a single shred of light.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, they're... sleepwalking? How do we wake them up?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...If we knew how, we would have done so back then.

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: G—Give us your worst! Kinkaku will never leave the Tanuki path! Kinkaku... Kinkaku will die before serving you!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I may have a solution.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Truly?

choices.text: If the nightmares come from the Abyss...

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: Wh—What are you doing...!? No... Don't!

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: ...The humans are everywhere. We can't hide forever...

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: How long have we been hiding? One hundred years? Five hundred years?

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: No idea... If Ioroi was still around, he would remember...

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: Quiet! Someone's coming!

response.speaker: Kaga
response.text: ...This is a fine piece of land! The grain yield should be exceptional.

response.speaker: Kiritani
response.text: Remember to check for traces of youkai in the surrounding area. By order of the Shogun...

response.speaker: Kiritani
response.text: ...By order of the Shogun, we are to exterminate all youkai that cross our path!

response.speaker: Mizukawa
response.text: Hah, why so hasty? We should leave some alive. We can make them work their own land, haha!

response.speaker: Kaga
response.text: Hey, you know about the Mikawa Flower Festival, right? I heard fifty percent of the profit is going to the development fund!

response.speaker: Mizukawa
response.text: Oh, yeah! The festival for humans and...

response.speaker: Mizukawa
response.text: ...The festival for humans and humans alone! Heh, the youkai have had their fun. It's our turn, now!

response.speaker: Kaga
response.text: That's right! We should put them to work! They're known for their transformations, right? Heh, then the little monkeys can dance for us until they die, haha...

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: N—No... How could they do that...

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: Quiet! O—Or they'll catch us...

response.speaker: Kiritani
response.text: Hahahahaha!

response.speaker: Kaga
response.text: What... What is that!? Argh!

response.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
response.text: Hey... Are you alright? Youko! Kappa! I need help over here!

response.speaker: Kappa
response.text: Hold on, we're coming... Arghhh!

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: The youkai... and the humans... are unconscious?

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: The same thing happened... to all of them?

response.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
response.text: ...The Mikawa Flower Festival...

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: This youkai... can speak!

response.speaker: Youko
response.text: No... If we don't make it to the Mikawa Flower Festival... Boss Thoma will be so upset...

response.speaker: Youko
response.text: ...Boss Thoma... will eat us...

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: EEEK!!!

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: The humans are coming for us... We're gonna lose our home... Wh—What do we do?

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: W—We infiltrate the Mikawa Flower Festival! We scare the humans away... Then, they won't come!

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: But, how do we get into the festival...?

response.speaker: Kappa
response.text: Boss Thoma... is the best...

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: How about... we turn into those three youkai...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (These memories... They belong to the bake-danuki...?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #...Are you alright, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I'm fine.

response.speaker: Tetsunosuke
response.text: Uh... Wh—Where are we...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Huh? The nightmare is gone! You... purified it?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just my way of dealing with the Abyss.

response.speaker: Ginkaku
response.text: Eek! H—Humans! And a bunch of youkai!

response.speaker: Kinkaku
response.text: The Mikawa Flower Festival! The humans are gonna... They're gonna... What were they gonna do?

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Looks like they're confused... They still seem wary of humans...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That might have something to do with a long time in hiding...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: ...Hiding?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe the memories to the group...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... That explains all the "Boss Thoma" this, and "Boss Thoma" that. That was the only thing they could imitate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a second, Hitotsume Kozou and the others should be Akitsu Yuugei experts. But, this time, Thoma did all the work! Paimon can't believe we missed something so suspicious!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're like Heizou, if his skills only worked in hindsight...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, you're saying Paimon's deductive reasoning is Heizou level!

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Heh, more or less.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: #Based on your description, {NICKNAME}, it's possible these bake-danuki have been in hiding for five hundred years... Sounds like they know Ioroi, too. Why don't we ask him? He's not far.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Protector of the Grove... It's been five hundred years since our last meeting. Sara, Heizou, return to the festival to keep watch.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: The Doppelganger incident has been resolved, but the threat of the Nightmare remains. I will handle the meeting with Ioroi myself.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou & Kujou Sara
response.text: Yes, Shogun!

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou & Kujou Sara
response.text: Yes, Shogun!

choices.text: There's something I can try...
Kichiboushi and the others weren't forced into anything...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ioroi! We're back!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: *snore*... Keep it down... Bringing all these people at this hour... Don't you know even statues... need to... sleep...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Sh—Shogun! I bow before thee... No, wait... Shoot! I'm still a statue... What should I—

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: All is well, Ioroi, Hidden Protector of the Grove.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've never seen Ioroi so afraid...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, that would be because, when Ioroi tried to pluck a Naku Weed from the imperial garden, Ei nearly split him in two... Yashiori Island style...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...Keep it to yourself, you meddlesome kitsune!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...Ioroi, I wish to ask you something.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...Anything, Shogun! Absolutely anything! It is my honor to answer!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh, suck-up...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Phew... You could have at least slowed down a little... It took forever to convince them to come with me...

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Ah! It's Ioroi!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: ...The humans really did kill you!

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: ...Your body is stone!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Huh!? I am not dead!

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: Not... dead? The kitsune spoke the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: This smell... is Ioroi! Ioroi is alive?

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: Ioroi! The humans really did seal you away!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Wait, this must be... Kinkaku... Ginkaku.... and Tetsunosuke? You weren't sealed away?

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Hmph... When the human, Kamuna Harunosuke, came to hurt us...

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: We ran and hid... The human searched and searched... So many friends couldn't move. Our youkai powers were getting weaker...

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: So, we decided to escape the human just as the great bake-danuki Tsukumo taught us — by digging a hole in the ground!

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: That's when we uncovered a horn filled with youkai power! It was the will of the great bake-danuki Giichiro made manifest!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: It restored our power! And we made the human go thump thump, clang clang, slash slash!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Ooh! And by thump thump, clang clang, slash slash, you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: ...We tricked him and ran!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...So, you didn't actually beat him up at all...

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: We've been using the horn to hide ever since... But, there are too many humans... It's getting harder to hide...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: A horn full of youkai power... Could that be the source of the nightmares? The reason the bake-danuki are so afraid of humans?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: If the horn contained the fragment of a nightmare, using its power to hide would spread the nightmare to them. That means, the bake-danuki have been trapped in this state of anxiety... for five hundred years...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Hah, I could have told you nothing good would come from that horn... Using external power is against the Tanuki path!

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: Eek! We... strayed from the path?

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: But... the horn helped us hide from the humans! The humans tried to take our land...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...On the contrary, the purpose of the investigation was to determine in advance if youkai were present on the land in question.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Whether we avoid encroaching on youkai territory altogether or attempt to reach a mutually beneficial agreement, a peaceful resolution was always the goal.

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Oh... really?

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: Wait... that IS what the human said back then, isn't it...

dialogues.speaker: Kiritani
dialogues.text: ...By order of the shogun, if youkai live here, we need to discuss the proposal...

talks.objective: Talk to Miko and the others

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Kinkaku, Ginkaku, Tetsunosuke... Not all humans are bad. Yellow Fur over there helped me a great deal, you know...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Besides, the bake-danuki were only sealed away back then because Ioroi stole that comb...

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Ioroi... is a thief? Ioroi... got what he deserved?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...H—H—How was I to know it was used to make Sacred Sakura Daifuku? I gave it back, didn't I!?

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: So, the humans were mean for no reason?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Well... if you must know, the young human and I fought... I was, perhaps, a tad careless, so I... conceded the match! Anyway, the point is... Neither side is bad!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There he goes again, changing the subject when it makes him look bad...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Now you know... No human is trying to harm you.

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: So... it was all a nightmare...

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: Five hundred years in hiding... for nothing...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: ...Eh, it was a five-hundred-year-long game of Hide-and-Seek. What's so bad about that? Besides, you won.

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: Huh? We won? ...Go us! We're even better than Ioroi!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Hey! My game of Hide-and-Seek isn't over yet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, the mind of a bake-danuki is something else... Still so cheerful, even after all that...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: That nature is what isolated them from the worst effects of the nightmare and prevented them from causing any real harm.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: But, a nightmare that's still affecting people after all this time? Who could it belong to? Hm, a horn buried under Mt. Yougou...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I feel like I've heard a legend about that...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Tainted by darkness, the oni warrior raised her sword against the Almighty Shogun. Losing an arm and a horn to the Shogun's blade, she fled into the forest, never to be seen again.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...A trusted lieutenant fighting against the forces of darkness, she was once devoured whole by a beast from beyond this world, with the body of a tiger and the tail of a serpent, until she tore the creature apart from within...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Thus, she earned the name, "Chiyo the Tiger-Bite"... Or, "Torachiyo."

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I don't think... Chiyo would like that name.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Though she escaped the belly of the beast alive... That battle never left her.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: She saw the memories of her fallen comrades everywhere, slaughtered one after another, until she could no longer distinguish dream from reality...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (A nightmare doesn't incapacitate someone with sufficient strength... It turns into something even worse...)

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...The nightmare twisted every joy in her life — her subordinates, family, and friends — into enemies in need of destruction.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: It was in that state, trapped in the battlefield of her mind, that she raised her sword against me on Mt. Yougou.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: With the Musou no Hitotachi, I cut off her arm, one of her horns, and a portion of the mountain itself... I suspect that is when the horn in question was buried there.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: And, subsequently, uncovered by three bake-danuki... That means the fragment on the horn... comes from Chiyo's nightmare.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #Nightmares feed on fear and anxiety. If what {NICKNAME} saw is true...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: It's possible Kinkaku and the others' fear over the past five hundred years allowed the fragment to gain physical form and become something akin to a jibakurei.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jibakurei?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: An earthbound spirit. They move through the Ley Lines, but are also bound by them. That's why the traces of this entity appeared intermittently, and never outside of Mt. Yougou.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: It would seem the fragment of this Nightmare is no different from the one back then... It hates all joy and every good thing in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The Investigation Team working for a better future? Attacked... Hitotsume Kozou and his friends, kind enough to lend a helping hand? Attacked...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, and we were attacked, too! Right when we were having fun with the play-testing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, why hasn't it appeared since?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
