dialogues.text: Perhaps it needs to regain strength after your defeat... Or, perhaps it is biding its time because it knows, with whatever rationality remains, that it cannot defeat you...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...But, sooner or later, its twisted hatred will force it out of hiding, and it will move to strike its "enemies."

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: When Chiyo set her sights on a target... She never was one to waver.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...But, both possibilities prove something... Nightmare Fragments can be defeated.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: And an enemy that can be killed... is one that can be split in two by the power of Musou Isshin.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...There's really no other way?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Mikoshi Chiyo is gone. A fragment of a Nightmare tied to a severed horn... That is all that remains. The living must take precedent over the memory of the dead.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Even so, having to unleash Musou Isshin against her again? Would Ei really be okay?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Mizuki said Archons suffer from the same turmoil as the rest of us... The dead may be gone, but that doesn't mean our emotions die with them...)

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Who cares about the dead, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: I'm just trying to look out for the living.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...! What is that supposed to mean, Miko?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm just concerned about our poor bake-danuki friends...

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Huh? What does this have to do with us?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: The Nightmare Fragment has been tied to the bake-danuki for nearly five hundred years. Strike it down, and who's to say whether you take the lives of our poor friends along with it.

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: EEEK!?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: I... I beseech you, Almighty Shogun! S—Spare the young ones! It was just a momentary... Or, uh, no... a five-hundred-year long lapse in judgement...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Miko... You speak the truth?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: #If you don't believe me, ask Mizuki and {NICKNAME}. I'm sure they've encountered similar cases during their extensive travels...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Well, I... Oh!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...Yes! During my studies, both in Liyue and Natlan!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah! I've definitely seen that happen before!

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Then... What would you propose? This Nightmare Fragment is a constant threat to Inazuma. Should all other options fail... I will take action.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...If the Fragment's hatred toward the world comes from a Nightmare, then the most logical option... is to get rid of the Nightmare itself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Right! Can't you just eat the Nightmare, Mizuki?

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...The Yumekui-Baku already tried that five hundred years ago. Even yesterday, when faced with the corruption of the Nightmare, Mizuki could only mitigate the effects.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: What was impossible back then... is not necessarily impossible now. I think Mizuki has the right idea. If we cannot eradicate the nightmares directly...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Why not use this entity's tricks against it? Combat illusions with illusions. Combat nightmares... with dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that even possible?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Don't forget — there are youkai that specialize in shapeshifting and illusions, and they happen to be right in front of us.

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: Wh—Where? Kinkaku doesn't see them anywhere!

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Maybe they're hiding as trees? Or the wind?

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Fools! The kitsune is clearly referring to the bake-danuki! Tetsunosuke, Kinkaku, must you be so dense!?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Given their centuries-long connection to the Nightmare Fragment, they are perfectly positioned to create a dreamscape that the entity will be unable to distinguish from the real world.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: ...Back then, the Nightmare had little to no weaknesses... If we want to give the bake-danuki an opportunity to strike, I assume you have a plan, Miko?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: You said it yourself — Mikoshi Chiyo is gone. All that remains is a fragment of her nightmare, already broken and vulnerable.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Besides... Mizuki is an old friend, one that is not to be underestimated. She has traveled the land studying dreams and is far more capable than those old fossils back then.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh... Um...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Not gonna say anything?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: She just... usually doesn't compliment me to my face... But, Miko's right. If we work together, I'm confident we can put together a ritual to subdue the Nightmare Fragment.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Once we perform the ritual, it will take some time for the barrier to take effect. Luckily for us, we have two formidable warriors on our side...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: ...Our festival representative, who also happens to have extensive experience against dark forces, and the Almighty Shogun, unmatched in combat... I'm sure the two of you can buy us some time?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: There's just one problem... Since this entity can pass through the Ley Lines, its movements are unpredictable. If we're going to create a barrier, how can we be sure it appears where we want?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, the solution to that... is obvious. If the Nightmare Fragment despises all sources of joy and happiness...

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Then, naturally, a joyous occasion would be an evil beyond measure — an enemy that must be annihilated at all costs...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: So, if we want to lure it out...

choices.text: We need a source of joy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...The Mikawa Flower Festival!

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hehe, what joy could possibly compare to finishing one's work right before the deadline?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...I would imagine we can all think of a few. But, I agree — the Mikawa Flower Festival is the most plausible target.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Once the enemy appears, I will pull them into the Plane of Euthymia immediately... I will not put the people in danger.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, I ask that you join me there so we can subdue the enemy together.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Alright, I will update everyone back at the festival and start the preparations for the ritual... I'll need your help, Mizuki. It's going to be a busy night.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Looks like another all-nighter for me.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: ...Well, this was your idea. Oh, and don't forget — you need to finish "A Little Fox's Daydream" as well.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...And, in a surprising twist, you were my nightmare all along!

choices.text: Then, the obvious target would be...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... During the battle tomorrow, it is imperative you know your limits. If the enemy proves too much to handle... leave them to me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But—

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: I know... I understand your concerns, just as you know mine. We need not say any more than that. Just get some rest and prepare yourself for the battle to come.

choices.text: Okay.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Ah, one more thing... Thank you.

choices.text: Get some rest, Ei.

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Well, shall we head out?

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: ...Kappa! Kappa!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Excuse me, let me take a look!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Mizuki? {NICKNAME}? Finally, you're back!

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: Shogun! ...The fault is mine. The Tenryou Commission failed to protect those under our charge...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Now is not the time to cast blame. Did anyone witness the attack?

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: ...No, we have failed you. There is no trace of the enemy...

dialogues.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
dialogues.text: We split up for just a second, and the next thing we knew, he was on the ground!

dialogues.speaker: Youko
dialogues.text: *whimper*... It... It must be some terrible youkai...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Other than the bake-danuki transformation, there was no trace of youkai power at the scene... It's almost like the culprit's methods are getting more sophisticated.

choices.text: The doppelganger in Inazuma City...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Wait... there was a doppelganger in Inazuma City?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, seems like it...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Doppelgangers... Nightmares... Inazuma City... Mt. Yougou...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: How is he, Mizuki?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: It's strange... I can't perceive his nightmare. It's almost like... he's not there at all.

response.speaker: Hitotsume Kozou
response.text: Th—The youkai... It must be getting stronger!

response.speaker: Youko
response.text: Kappa... *whimper*... Please don't die...

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...It's my fault! I should have anticipated the culprit might resort to more sophisticated methods...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: No, it was I who underestimated the enemy... I who allowed us to continue the festival despite the potential dangers.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Sara, what is the status of the other contestants and staff?

response.speaker: Kujou Sara
response.text: ...All normal. I asked the Yashiro Commission to move them to a secure location just to be safe.

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: Good... By decree of the Shogun, I declare that the Mikawa Flower Festival is—

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Wait...

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: What is it, Miko?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You're being too hasty, Ei. I understand your concern for the people, but I urge you to think this through, or we risk playing into the enemy's hand.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Considering your history with Nightmares, you have better cause than anyone to exercise caution... But, do you truly believe what we're facing now... is just a Nightmare?

response.speaker: Ei
response.text: ...Explain.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Call it intuition... If you want the truth, perhaps Doushin Shikanoin could shed some light. I believe there's been a break in the case.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: ...You flatter me, Lady Guuji. I do have a few ideas...

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Up to this point, we've only detected traces of the nightmare creature around Mt. Yougou... And, now, a doppelganger appears in Inazuma City.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Our original thought was that the culprit infiltrated the venue to evade capture... If so, there would be no reason for them to risk exposure by continuing to change form.

response.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
response.text: Rather than concluding that the nightmare creature, on top of everything, now has the ability to disappear without a trace, I think there's a different possibility...

choices.text: Also seemed to appear without warning...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet...

dialogues.speaker: Ei
dialogues.text: Not a problem. I'll wait here.

dialogues.speaker: Tetsunosuke
dialogues.text: Great youkai really wasn't forced to work all night?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: That's right. It was my choice.

dialogues.speaker: Kinkaku
dialogues.text: Why does great youkai have to work?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...I suppose it's just the price of becoming a great youkai.

dialogues.speaker: Ginkaku
dialogues.text: Great youkai, Ginkaku is sad for you...

dialogues.speaker: Shikanoin Heizou
dialogues.text: Interesting... The culprit's motive and method all seem rather self-contradictory. But, when did we first notice the dissonance...

dialogues.speaker: Kujou Sara
dialogues.text: It's rare to see the Almighty Shogun in such a good mood... Hmph, I will not let some wretched miscreant undermine the festival.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: An enemy that has two different abilities and can suddenly appear and disappear without a trace... It seems too random, like a novel from Yae Publishing House that tries to incorporate every element under the sun.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The nightmare creature and the doppelgangers... are separate entities. That's why their methods are so different. They have separate goals.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The people who saw doppelgangers were mistaken and the nightmare I saw wasn't real... No, no. I can't just explain it away...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound right... I need to think about this some more.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We thought the culprit was changing form to evade capture... But, if the doppelganger isn't responsible for the nightmares, they would be no more deserving of arrest than a random prankster...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The doppelganger incident didn't actually hurt anyone... But, the folk tale about doppelgangers did cause people to panic... That must be the culprit's goal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Taking control of Inazuma by replacing everyone with doppelgangers... I doubt even a folk tale would come up with something so unrealistic.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound right... I need to think about this some more.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Looks like everyone's busy trying to finish their game... I should come back later.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Man, what happened last night? We couldn't find anyone to discuss it with because it was so late... Well, Miko and the others should be at the grounds by now, right? Let's go talk to them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, so where do we start... We need to ask questions to figure out if there's an imposter, but we can't arouse suspicion...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, looks like Sayu's team is already here. Well, guess we'll just... play it by ear.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... Another day of hard work. Where did the time go...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? When did Ei get ahead of us? Let's catch up!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Bake-danuki, those little terrors... C'mon, let's go after them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! We must be in the wrong spot! They probably didn't make it this far.
